title: Batch Discussion overlap reads with complete pagination
body:
Discussion scans currently make a separate comments request for every thread, including empty threads. This change includes the first five comments and replies in each 50-thread listing and exhausts the remaining cursors in 100-item pages. It preserves ordered records, search behavior, cache lifetime and replacement only after a complete fetch.

On the same 20 public Discussions, three alternating before/after pairs returned all 77 records with identical hashes. Requests fell from **21 to 2** per run; median wall time fell from **18.44 to 2.63 seconds**, with ranges 17.64–18.52 and 2.59–3.25 seconds. The [evidence package](https://github.com/arhamgarg/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a459ee34fad0488691beba8441e0a31e103b91a5/research/overlap-discussion-batching/README.md) includes the runnable opt-in benchmark, every measurement, source pins and an offline replay.

Validation on Python 3.12.13, macOS arm64:

- `uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py' -v`: 71 tests, 68 passed and three Linux-only checks skipped.
- `uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/overlap-discussion-batching`: six coverage tests pass normally and under `-O`; metadata/source checks pass.
- The request-budget test fails on base with `53 != 2`. Stopping either comment or reply pagination causes the CLI coverage test to fail. Later-page errors preserve old complete evidence and its timestamp.
- `git diff --check` and the selected source-binding baseline pass. The final live overlap scan covered 687 open PRs and 1,199 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings.

This is a **draft because two affected older replay packages fail their frozen source checks on both untouched main and this branch**. `overlap-path-index` reports a source-blob provenance mismatch; `research-package-pin-batching` reports onboarding-test drift. This patch also changes the onboarding bytes pinned by the first package. The README records exact commands and errors. Their pins remain unchanged under repository guidance; integration needs a maintainer source-binding decision. Aaron Wang's [PR2255](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2255) documents the broader existing issue.

The task picker selected verifier engineering, `replay-runtime`, at priority revision 4. TASK.json declares the change in scope to the required overlap step, prompted by measured scan cost and public stall reports. Base is `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. Coordination is in [Discussion2264](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2264). [PR2154](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2154) changes task-term extraction and is a distinct contribution, with no dependency.

Timing is corpus and environment dependent. GitHub pagination remains non-atomic during concurrent edits; very busy threads may need an extra continuation. No full supplier replay, Linux timing, mathematical advance or selected-frontier change is claimed. No existing files or functions were deleted. Hosted CI has been triggered and remains queued as of 2026-10-15 12:43 UTC. No remote check is claimed as passing; the [registered-package run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38736581121) selects this package and the two frozen dependents above.

Credit to Douglas Colkitt and the overlap-tool contributors, including Nick Petalas's pagination compatibility repair. Prepared by Arham Garg with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, GPT-6 Astra, for implementation, verification and writing. No independent review is claimed. Apache-2.0.
